prompt: `LLMClient` is the abstract base class for LLM providers. Which other entities in this codebase serve a similar role — i.e. they are abstract base classes for pluggable external service providers, but for different domains? Return one qualified entity name per line.

ground_truth.notes:
Class D cross-file relatedness, mixed-favored a priori.

LLMClient is an ABC in src/loomgraph/llm/base.py — abstract `complete(prompt) -> str`. Two sibling ABCs play the same architectural role in different domains:
- `GraphStore` in storage/base.py — abstract async graph storage API (13 methods), implemented by SqliteGraphStore
- `EmbeddingClient` in embedding/base.py — abstract embedding API, implemented by DirectEmbeddingClient

These 3 ABCs are the explicit architectural pattern. Path A README_AI for each subdir should describe them. Path B can discover via topology / find queries but linking the concept requires reasoning.

Verified: `grep -rn 'class.*ABC' src/loomgraph/` shows these 3 plus a few internal mixins. The 3 listed are the production provider-pattern ABCs.

rationale: Class D — cross-module pattern recognition. The 3 ABC providers (LLM / GraphStore / Embedding) form an explicit architectural pattern documented in ADRs. Tests whether each path can identify the pattern across separate module READMEs (Path A) or by traversing similar source_id prefixes (Path B).
